question.text:
Let $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $y \in \mathbb{R}.$ Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\forall \, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, 2y=0.$
  2. The truth set of the predicate $\big( \, \forall y \in \mathbb{R}, \, xy=0 \, \big)$ is $\emptyset.$
  3. $\exists \, x \in \mathbb{R}, \, \forall y \in \mathbb{R}, \, xy=0.$
question.choice5: None of the statements are true
question.explanation:
First, notice that the statement

\[ \exists \, x \in \mathbb{R}, \, \forall y \in \mathbb{R}, \, xy=0 \]

from option III reads as follows:

$\qquad$ There exists a real $x$ such that, for every real $y,$ we have $xy=0.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is false since $2y=0$ is not true for some real $y.$ Say, for $y=1.$

  • Statement II is false. The predicate \[ P(x): \quad \forall\, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, xy=0 \] is true for some $x\in\mathbb R.$ For example, \[ P(0) : \quad \forall\, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, 0\cdot y=0 \] is true. Therefore, its truth set is not empty.

  • Statement III is true. The sentence \[ \big( \,\exists \, x \in \mathbb{R}, \, \forall y \in \mathbb{R}, \, xy=0 \, \big) \] can be written as \[ \exists \, x \in \mathbb{R} \, \big( \, \underbrace{\forall y \in \mathbb{R}, \, xy=0}_{P(x)} \, \big) \] which is true whenever the inner predicate $P(x)$ has a nonempty truth set. And according to statement II, this is the case.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

example.title: Finding the Truth Value of a Statement Involving Nested Quantifiers

question.text:
Let $x \in \mathbb{R}$ and $y \in \mathbb{R}.$ Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\exists\, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, 1-2y=0.$
  2. The truth set of the predicate $\big( \, \exists\, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, x-2y=0 \, \big)$ is $\mathbb{R}.$
  3. $\exists\, x,y \in \mathbb{R}, \, x-2y =0 .$
question.explanation:
First, notice that the statement

\[ \exists\, x,y \in \mathbb{R}, \, x-2y =0 \]

from option III reads as follows:

$\qquad$ There exist reals $x$ and $y,$ such that $x- 2y =0.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is true, $1-2y=0$ for some real number $y$ (e.g., for $y=\dfrac{1}{2}$)

  • Statement II is true. For the predicate \[ P(x): \quad \exists\, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, x- 2y=0 \] we note that $P(x)$ is true for any real $x.$ For example, \[ P(1) : \quad \exists\, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, 1 - 2y=0 \] is true for the statement I. Similarly, \[ P(2) : \quad \exists\, y \in \mathbb{R}, \, 2- 2y = 0 \] is true, since we can take $y=1.$ And so on. In general, it's sufficient to take $y=\dfrac{x}{2}.$

  • Statement III is true. The sentence \[ \big( \, \exists\, x,y \in \mathbb{R}, \, x-2y=0 \, \big) \] can be written as \[ \exists x \in \mathbb{R} \, \big( \, \underbrace{\exists y \in \mathbb{R}, \, x- 2y=0}_{P(x)} \, \big) \] which is true whenever the inner predicate $P(x)$ has a nonempty truth set. And according to statement II, this is the case.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III."

example.title: Finding the Truth Value of a Statement Involving Nested Quantifiers

question.text:
Let $p \in \mathbb{Q}$ and $q \in \mathbb{Q}.$ Which of the following statements are true?

  1. $\exists\, p \in \mathbb{Q}, \, 2p=-1.$
  2. The truth set of the predicate $\big( \, \exists\, p \in \mathbb{Q}, \, p\cdot q=-1 \, \big)$ is $\mathbb{Q}.$
  3. $\exists\, q, p \in \mathbb{Q}, \, p\cdot q=-1.$
question.explanation:
First, notice that the statement

\[ \exists\, q,p \in \mathbb{Q}, \, p\cdot q=-1 \]

from option III reads as follows:

$\qquad$ There exist rationals $q$ and $p,$ such that $p \cdot q=-1.$

With that in mind, let's examine our statements in turn.

  • Statement I is true, $2p=-1$ for some rational number $p$ (e.g., for $p=-\dfrac{1}{2}$).

  • Statement II is false. For the predicate \[ P(q): \quad \exists\, p \in \mathbb{Q}, \, p\cdot q=-1 \] we note that $P(q)$ is true for some $q\in\mathbb Q$ and false for others. For example, \[ P(0) : \quad \exists\, p \in \mathbb{Q}, \, p\cdot 0 =-1 \] is false. However, \[ P(1) : \quad \exists\, p \in \mathbb{Q}, \, p \cdot 1 =-1 \] is true, since we can take $p=-1.$

  • Statement III is true. The sentence \[ \big( \, \exists\, q, p \in \mathbb{Q}, \, p\cdot q=-1 \, \big) \] can be written as \[ \exists q \in \mathbb{Q} \, \big( \, \underbrace{\exists p \in \mathbb{Q}, \, p\cdot q=-1}_{P(q)} \, \big) \] which is true whenever the inner predicate $P(q)$ has a nonempty truth set. And according to the discussion in statement II, this is the case.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."

example.title: Finding the Truth Value of a Statement Involving Nested Quantifiers

question.text:
\[ \forall \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\text{I}}}{w} \in \mathbb{Z}, \, \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\text{II}}}{w} \mid ( \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\text{III}}}{x}+3) \]

Which occurrences of the variables in the expression above are free?
question.explanation:
Let's examine our expression and mark the occurrences of the variables as bound $(\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\small\text{b}})$ or free $(\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\small\text{f}}).$

  • Occurrence I of the variable $w$ is bound since it's placed right next to the quantifier $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\forall}{:}$ \[ \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\forall} \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{w} \in \mathbb{Z}, \, w \mid (x+3) \]

  • Occurrence II of the variable $w$ is bound since it lies within the scope of the quantifier $\forall w$ that uses $w{:}$ \[ \forall w \in \mathbb{Z}, \, \overbrace{ \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{w} \mid (x+3) }^{\textrm{scope of $\forall w$}} \]

  • Occurrence III of the variable $x$ is free since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $x.$

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows: \[ \forall \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{w} \in \mathbb{Z}, \, \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{w} \mid ( \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\text{f}}}}{x} + 3) \]

Therefore, the free occurrence is "III only."

example.title: Identifying Free and Bound Occurrences of Variables

question.text:
\[ \big( \, \forall y \in (0,1), \, \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[3pt] \uparrow \\[5pt] \large\text{I}}}{x^2} - y^2 \geq 0 \, \big) \Rightarrow \big( \, \exists \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\text{II}}}{z} \in \mathbb{Q}, \, {z} = \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[3pt] \uparrow \\[5pt] \large\text{III}}}{y^2} \, \big) \]

Which occurrences of the variables in the expression above are free?
question.explanation:
Let's examine our expression and mark the occurrences of the variables as bound $(\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\small\text{b}})$ or free $(\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\small\text{f}}).$

  • Occurrence I of the variable $x$ is free since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $x.$

  • Occurrence II of the variable $z$ is bound since it is placed right next to the quantifier $\bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\exists}{:}$ \[ \big({\forall}y \in (0,1), \, {x^2 - y^2 \geq 0} \, \big) \Rightarrow \big( \, \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{\exists} \! \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[6pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{z} \in \mathbb{Q}, \, {z} = {y^2} \, \big) \]

  • Occurrence III of the variable $y$ is free since it isn't placed right next to a quantifier and it doesn't lie within the scope of a quantifier that uses $y.$

The occurrences of variables in the expression are as follows: \[ \big( \, \forall \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[3pt] \uparrow \\[5pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{y} \in (0,1), \, { \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[5pt] \uparrow \\[7pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\text{f}}}}{x^2} -{\underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[5pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{y^2}} \geq 0 } \, \big) \Rightarrow \big( \, \exists \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[7pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{z} \in \mathbb{Q}, \, \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[7pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,Moccasin]{\text{b}}}}{z} = \underset{\substack{\phantom{.} \\[4pt] \uparrow \\[5pt] \large\phantom{.}\bbox[2pt,LightBlue]{\text{f}}}}{y^2} \, \big) \]

Therefore, the free occurrence is "I and III only."
